proposition: Artifact similarity does not uniquely establish derivation direction
counter_history: common predecessor, shared library, common template, legitimate version, or independent implementation
boundary: Analytical non-identifiability claim supported by explicit original/direction limitations. Chronology, market labels or ownership heuristics alone do not exclude a common predecessor.

proposition: Component presence does not establish application ancestry exact version reachability or exploitability
counter_history: fork, shaded dependency, partial inclusion, vendor patch, dead code, dynamic loading, or database gap
boundary: Report candidate sets, inclusion evidence, reference date, reachability and environment separately; static reachability does not certify actual invocation.

proposition: Authenticated process provenance does not establish benign behavior
counter_history: a compromised or policy-approved workflow can faithfully produce a malicious artifact
boundary: Bind the exact artifact to a separate behavior-specific property and analysis model; artifact/operation/actor properties are explicit antecedents.

proposition: A valid signature does not automatically establish authorization under the relevant policy
counter_history: stolen key, expired role, wrong namespace, compromised account, or policy change
boundary: Name principal role, scope, validity interval and policy version; configured key identity is not authenticated real-person identity.

proposition: Reproducible bytes do not establish approval or acceptable inputs
counter_history: independent builders can reproduce the same unauthorized or vulnerable source and dependencies
boundary: Analytical counter-history, not a measured new result. DetTrace assumes supported Linux/x86-64 execution and declared initial state; CHAINIAC assumes secure bootstrap and honest verification thresholds. Equality, approval and behavior remain separate.

proposition: A generation log is not automatically a complete causal history
counter_history: hidden retrieval, rejected outputs, tool state, model drift, or human edits can affect the accepted change
boundary: Analytical causal-record requirement inferred from generation steps and snapshot limits, not an empirical claim that the cited systems measured all hidden contexts.

proposition: Cross-layer assurance requires object predecessor principal and policy bindings
counter_history: evidence layers may describe different APKs components principals times or policies
boundary: Android-focused proposed binding discipline building on checked supply-chain properties/frameworks, not an evaluated architecture or verified novelty claim.
